title: Concentration-Risk Lineage Tracer: How Many 'Independent' Models Share a Base?

original_idea.body:
# Concentration-Risk Lineage Tracer: How Many 'Independent' Models Share a Base?

**Problem:** Success state: a deployer choosing several 'different' models for redundancy can verify they are genuinely independent rather than fine-tunes of the same base (hidden concentration risk). Backward: we need a lightweight fingerprinting method to detect shared lineage among open-weight models.

**Direction:** Build a behavioral fingerprint from each model's responses on a fixed probe set (idiosyncratic completions, tokenizer quirks, refusal phrasings, memorized strings). Cluster ~20 popular open models and check whether the behavioral clusters recover known shared-base lineages (e.g., Llama-derived fine-tunes). Report how often nominally distinct models cluster together — a measure of latent concentration.

**Why it matters:** The International AI Safety Report flags concentration risk from dependence on few foundation providers. A practical lineage tracer lets auditors detect when 'diverse' redundant systems are actually correlated, exposing systemic single-point-of-failure risk that marketing labels hide.

**Relevant context:** Targets the concentration-risk open problem (International AI Safety Report 2026). Uses only open-weight inference; behavioral fingerprinting needs no internal weights access.
